scope.description: Observe the removed-leader ReadIndex path when only PreVote is enabled: the same three-voter removal leaves a single-voter configuration, the remaining voter becomes leader and commits an entry, the removed leader answers a read before its next heartbeat tick, and the observations continue after that tick.
assumptions: Three voters {1,2,3} with PreVote enabled on every node and CheckQuorum disabled; node 1 is elected leader, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, and node 2 then becomes leader of {2} and commits one entry.
The read is delivered to node 1 before it has contacted the new leader, then one heartbeat tick is delivered to node 1 and its messages are pumped, and then a second read is delivered.

basis.prefix: Elect node 1 in {1,2,3} with a real MsgHup/MsgVote round, apply the committed removal of node 1 on all nodes, elect node 2 in {2} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, deliver one heartbeat tick of node 1 and pump its messages, then deliver a second MsgReadIndex to node 1.
basis.requirement: A ReadIndex answer must let the application serve a linearizable read (raft.go:233-244 and README.md:27-32 state that ReadOnlySafe achieves linearizability by communicating with the quorum, and node.go:218-224 states that once the application advances past the returned read index, linearizable reads issued before the request can be processed safely). The tracker's own comment for IsSingleton says the single voting member is the leader, so answering locally without any check is only sound when that member is the local node.
basis.responsibility: raft (target): the singleton shortcut in the ReadIndex path decides the answer for the whole configuration, and message handling decides whether the removed leader learns of the new term.

comparisons.description: Premise: with PreVote enabled the removal still leaves node 1 leading a configuration whose single voter is node 2.
Premise: the new leader of {2} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Witness before the step-down: with PreVote only, the removed leader answers with index 2 below the committed index 4 of the actual leader.
Bound: one heartbeat tick is enough for the step-down, matching the guard (checkQuorum || preVote) on messages from a lower term.
After the step-down the same request is no longer answered, so PreVote alone bounds the exposure.

before.description: Observe the removed-leader ReadIndex path in four configurations of the same removal: a single-voter remainder, a two-voter remainder, a single-voter remainder with CheckQuorum enabled, and a single-voter remainder with PreVote enabled and CheckQuorum disabled.
assumptions: Scenarios in one process: voters {1,2} where the removal leaves {2}; voters {1,2,3} where the removal leaves {2,3}; and voters {1,2} with Config.CheckQuorum true on both nodes; ReadOnlySafe and StepDownOnRemoval false in all of them.

In each scenario node 1 is elected leader, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on every node, the remaining voters then elect node 2 and commit one entry, and only then is the ReadIndex request delivered to node 1.

In the CheckQuorum scenario the observations are taken before and after the first heartbeat tick of the removed leader, so the receipt covers both the window in which the stale answer is issued and the state after the step-down.

In the PreVote scenario the observations are taken before and after the first heartbeat tick of the removed leader, as in the CheckQuorum scenario, so the receipt covers the window in which the stale answer is issued and the state after the step-down.
excluded: Snapshot transfer and asynchronous storage writes.

assumptions: Three voters {1,2,3} with PreVote enabled on every node and CheckQuorum disabled; node 1 is elected leader, the application proposes and applies the committed removal of node 1 on all three nodes, and node 2 then becomes leader of {2} and commits one entry.
The read is delivered to node 1 before it has contacted the new leader, then one heartbeat tick is delivered to node 1 and its messages are pumped, and then a second read is delivered.

prefix.before: Scenario A (single-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2}, apply the committed removal of node 1, elect node 2 in {2} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, deliver the same request to node 2, run three heartbeat intervals on node 1 and deliver a second MsgReadIndex to node 1. Scenario B (two-voter remainder): elect node 1 in {1,2,3}, apply the committed removal on all three nodes, elect node 2 in {2,3} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, then run three heartbeat intervals on node 1. Scenario C (single-voter remainder with CheckQuorum): as scenario A with Config.CheckQuorum true, but the read is delivered before the removed leader has contacted the new leader, then one heartbeat tick is delivered and the step-down is observed, then a further MsgReadIndex is delivered. Scenario D (single-voter remainder with PreVote and without CheckQuorum): as scenario C, but the read is delivered before the removed leader has contacted the new leader, then one heartbeat tick is delivered and the step-down is observed, then a further MsgReadIndex is delivered.
prefix.after: Elect node 1 in {1,2,3} with a real MsgHup/MsgVote round, apply the committed removal of node 1 on all nodes, elect node 2 in {2} and commit one proposal, deliver MsgReadIndex to node 1, deliver one heartbeat tick of node 1 and pump its messages, then deliver a second MsgReadIndex to node 1.

responsibility.before: raft (target): the singleton shortcut in the ReadIndex path decides the answer for the whole configuration, and the library already refuses proposals from a leader that is not in its own configuration.
responsibility.after: raft (target): the singleton shortcut in the ReadIndex path decides the answer for the whole configuration, and message handling decides whether the removed leader learns of the new term.

before.description: Scenario A premise: the node whose removal the application applied is still leading a configuration whose single voter is another node.
Scenario A premise: the actual leader of the reduced configuration has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Scenario A witness: the removed leader answered the read with an index below the commit index of the actual leader, sending no message at all.
Scenario A control: the same request answered by the actual leader returns an index that covers its commit index.
Scenario A persistence: after three heartbeat intervals without replies the removed leader repeats the same stale index.
Scenario B premise: the same removal leaves a configuration with two voters, so the singleton shortcut cannot apply to the removed leader (config voters=(2 3)).
Scenario B premise: the new leader of {2,3} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.

Scenario B control outcome: the same read delivered to the removed leader produces no answer at all, and the leader instead enters the readOnly round (heartbeats_emitted 2 with a read context) - the stale immediate answer is specific to the singleton configuration.

Scenario B second symptom: the accepted read stays in readOnly.unconfirmed_reads because the current configuration never acknowledges the removed leader's old-term heartbeats, so no repair exists for it inside raft.
Scenario B persistence: three further heartbeat intervals still produce no answer and no reply from the current configuration.
Scenario C premise: with CheckQuorum enabled the removal still leaves node 1 leading a configuration whose single voter is node 2, so the shortcut applies.
Scenario C premise: the new leader of {2} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
Scenario C witness before the step-down: enabling CheckQuorum does not remove the stale answer - the removed leader still answers with index 2 below the committed index 4 of the actual leader.
Scenario C mitigation: the current leader answers the removed leader's old-term heartbeat with its higher term, so the removed leader becomes a follower (lead None) after one heartbeat tick.
Scenario C bound: the stale-answer window is at most the heartbeat interval - one tick was enough for the step-down in the exercised configuration.
Scenario C after the step-down: the same request is no longer answered (it is dropped because the node has no leader), so the exposure is bounded by the step-down rather than repaired inside raft.
PreVote premise: the removal still leaves node 1 leading a configuration whose single voter is node 2, so the shortcut applies.
PreVote premise: the new leader of {2} has committed an entry the removed leader's commit index does not cover.
PreVote witness before the step-down: with PreVote only the removed leader still answers with index 2 below the committed index 4 of the actual leader.
PreVote bound: one heartbeat tick is enough for the step-down, matching the guard (checkQuorum || preVote) on messages from a lower term.
PreVote after the step-down: the same request is no longer answered, so PreVote alone bounds the exposure as the source predicts.

revision_reason: The PreVote scenario now has its own self-contained harness and its own comparisons instead of sharing one prerequisite set with the other three scenarios, because the four-scenario basis left its new comparisons unknown (missing indices pointing at unmatched events of the last scenario). The harness contains only the PreVote scenario and copies the helpers it needs, so each alias's event appears exactly once.
